task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-19, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Opponent next-possession PPP after you run play X is large enough to drive AVOID labels; own-sequence lags similarly matter.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: derived play-type possession records from play-by-play
methodological_questions: Can opponent next-possession PPP after play X be estimated reliably enough to drive AVOID labels?
Do own-sequence lagged outcomes add predictive or diagnostic value beyond the current possession?
How do outcome-derived play-type labels bias evaluation of their own downstream PPP?
What sample sizes and exposure thresholds are needed for stable per-play-type PPP estimates?
Is there leakage when labels and next-possession outcomes are built from the same play-by-play?
evidence_establishes: No historical evidence was returned by retrieve_history for this question (n_results = 0), so no earlier study by this project is available to rely on for this question.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether opponent next-possession PPP after play X differs enough to justify AVOID labels.
Whether the derived play-type labels in [source] database are valid, reliable, or free of outcome contamination.
Any sample-size, exposure, or power figures for play-type PPP estimates in this project's data.
own_inferences: The question is answerable in principle: the play-by-play supplies action types, clock, score, and points, so next-possession outcomes can be built for each opponent possession.
The main threat is circularity. If AVOID labels are derived from the same next-possession points they are then evaluated against, the test is partly tautological.
Rare play types and small exposure counts per team or season will make per-type PPP noisy, so reliability must be checked before any label threshold is set.
Opponent lineup and quality effects, score state, and garbage time could confound any apparent PPP difference after play X.
Lag effects will be hard to separate from the current play's effect without a pre-specified lag structure.
uncertainties: No prior-study results, power calculations, or reliability estimates were retrieved.
The exact definition of AVOID and its threshold is not stated in the task.
It is unclear whether the derived possession records in [source] database have been validated against raw play-by-play.
The 2025-26 playoffs are partial before 2026-06-21, so they cannot be used as a complete holdout on the stated date.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval returned no records, so the decision rests on the task statement and the data description alone. No earlier result changed the decision.

blocking_constraints.text: AVOID labels are derived from the same next-possession PPP that the question evaluates; the test must use labels built without the outcome, or the effect is circular.
Play types and opponent-specific cells may have too few possessions per season for stable PPP estimates; minimum counts must be checked before analysis.
The power to detect a PPP difference large enough to drive labels has not been established; a pre-analysis power calculation is required.
Opponent lineup, matchup, score margin, and clock effects can produce apparent PPP differences after play X without any causal effect of the play.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved (n_results = 0). Whether this question has already been answered is unknown. No prior result is relied on here.

risks.text: If AVOID is defined using next-possession points, evaluating PPP against AVOID is circular. Labels must be fixed from pre-outcome information or from a separate season.
Building labels or features from the full play-by-play can use future possessions or the outcome of the possession being predicted. Features must use only information available before play X.
Rare play types or team-season cells may have too few possessions, making PPP estimates and the AVOID threshold unstable.
Play-type and initiator labels from [source] database may be noisy; their agreement with raw play-by-play has not been shown.
Opponent quality, lineup, score state, garbage time, and pace may drive PPP differences that are not caused by play X.
Selecting play types with extreme observed PPP and then reporting that PPP will overstate the effect (regression to the mean).
Testing many play types, lags, and thresholds raises false positives unless corrected.
Effects may appear whenever the placebo or baseline is weak; falsification tests are needed to show the effect is specific to play X.
Scoring and play-type usage changed across 2022-23 to 2025-26; a pooled estimate may hide season-specific shifts.
Overall league PPP sets the reference level; a small absolute PPP difference can look large relative to a low base rate, so thresholds must be stated in absolute points.

design.estimand: Difference in mean opponent next-possession PPP following play X versus matched baseline possessions, plus the incremental effect of lagged own-sequence outcomes, estimated on held-out data with labels fixed before outcome evaluation.
design.unit: Possession-level event: each opponent possession immediately following a play-type X event, with own-sequence lag features computed only from earlier possessions.
design.sample: Derivation: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25 regular season and playoffs. Holdout: 2025-26 regular season, using only the complete snapshot from 2026-04-13. Exclude 2025-26 playoffs until complete (2026-06-21). Include only play types and team-season cells that meet a minimum possession count set before analysis.
design.power: Before analysis, compute the minimum detectable absolute PPP difference for each play type given expected counts and the observed variance of possession points. Report the minimum detectable effect, and do not interpret effects below it.
design.controls: Adjust for score margin, game clock and period, opponent lineup and matchup minutes, possession start type, pace, and season fixed effects. Use shrinkage or hierarchical estimates for sparse cells. Lag features use only information from before play X.
design.falsification: Placebo play types with no hypothesized effect; permuted opponent identity; the same analysis on pre-play windows; an outcome-independent label check showing AVOID does not change when next-possession points are removed from the label construction.
design.multiplicity: Holm or Benjamini-Hochberg correction across play types and lag windows; the number of tested contrasts is recorded in advance.
design.decision_rule: Label AVOID only if, on the 2025-26 regular season holdout, the lower 95% bound of the adjusted PPP difference exceeds a pre-specified absolute threshold, the effect replicates in the derivation seasons, placebo and falsification tests show no effect, and the label is built from pre-outcome information. Otherwise report the question as inconclusive, not supported.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 through 2024-25 regular season and playoffs (complete); NBA 2025-26 regular season complete snapshot from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs excluded until complete on 2026-06-21. Derived play-type records from [source] database must be versioned and checked against raw play-by-play before use.
